title: SkeletonKey Skill frontmatter
description: The YAML header of skills/<name>/SKILL.md. A skill is instruction payload first and a tool manifest second: the loader injects the body (bounded by skills.max_inline_tokens) when a task matches, and registers any tool.toml candidates as hidden (advertised=false) entries so the registry already knows about them before Phase 2 synthesis exists. Unknown keys are ignored, not fatal - a skill written for a future version must still load today.

name.description: kebab-case. Defaults to the directory name; a frontmatter `name` wins over the directory, and if two skills resolve to one name the first directory wins and the loser is annotated in `parse_notes` ("shadowed by earlier ...") rather than silently replacing it.

description.description: One line. This is what the matcher shows the model when it is deciding whether to open the skill at all.

when_to_use.description: The trigger sentence. Matched as tokens against the task text, so write it in the agent's vocabulary ('renaming a symbol across the repo'), not in yours.

triggers.description: Explicit aliases; wins over when_to_use for matching if both are present.

priority.description: Breaks ties when several skills match one task, and decides who gets the last of the token budget.

requires.description: Capability or tool ids. A skill whose requirements this host fails is skipped rather than injected - half a procedure is worse than none.

disable_for.description: Os/tool exclusions, e.g. ["windows"] for a bash-only recipe.

allowed-tools.description: The tool ids this skill's procedure assumes. Reported in `skills.load` so a host can pre-approve exactly that set instead of the whole toolkit.

disabled.description: Not a frontmatter key: switch a skill off by naming its directory with a leading underscore (`skills/_draft-foo/`). The loader marks it disabled and `skills.list` shows why.

x-directory-convention.references/*.md: read on demand - `skills.load {references: [...]}` inlines selected files
x-directory-convention.scripts/*: executable helpers the procedure calls via shell.run
